explanation: Kanban incidents test one habit: finish before you start. The board's columns and WIP limit tell you exactly where defective work belongs.
instructions: You are on a team with a WIP limit of 3. 'Search Courses' is Done — but a user reports it crashes on empty queries. Decide what happens next.

options.label: Pull fresh work into Coding anyway
options.note: Starting new work while a defect escapes violates finish-before-start.

options.label: Move the card back to Coding/Testing and fix it within WIP
options.note: Done means accepted — a defective card re-enters the flow.

options.label: Ask to raise the WIP limit so everything fits
options.note: Raising WIP hides the constraint instead of resolving it.

alert.text: Bug report lands: 'Search Courses' (in Done) crashes on empty queries. Review is full (3/3), Coding has 1 card. What do you do first?

options.label: Merge it straight to Done — it was Done before
options.note: Fixes re-break things; the lecture says regressions re-occur.

options.label: Let it flow through Review and Awaiting Merge again

fixing.text: The card is back in Coding/Testing and the crash is fixed. Review still holds 3 cards. How does the fix reach Done?

limit.debrief: A WIP limit you raise whenever it binds is decoration. The pile-up was the diagnosis; the fix was rebalancing toward Review.
limit.text: The board absorbs everything — columns swell to 5, 6, 7 cards. Nothing finishes; the pile-up signal is gone.
limit.title: Limit inflated

rushed.debrief: WIP limits exist to force finishing over starting. New work while a known defect escapes multiplies rework.
rushed.text: Two streams now compete: the defect and the new feature. Review stays clogged; the crash reaches more users.
rushed.title: Split focus

sloppy.debrief: Regression discipline is the point of the Review column. Every fix gets re-reviewed, or Done stops meaning accepted.
sloppy.text: The fix ships unreviewed and breaks saved searches. Another card travels backwards — the team now distrusts Done.
sloppy.title: Unreviewed merge

solid.debrief: Move Done defects back, respect WIP, re-review fixes. That is the whole Kanban contract in one incident.
solid.text: Re-reviewed, re-merged, re-accepted. The board kept flowing because the team finished the defect before starting anything new.
solid.title: Discipline held
